reason: The hypothesis relies on a glass-to-glass transition mechanism from E2/E3, but those studies involve a different alloy (NbNiZrTiCo) and a distinct phenomenon (a high-energy to low-energy glass transition with massive heat release, not a simple sub-Tg relaxation). The cited evidence does not show that a sub-Tg anneal in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 induces a glass-to-glass transition or improves stability; E1 only confirms the alloy can be made amorphous. The key premise that a glass-to-glass transition will occur in this alloy under the proposed conditions is unsupported by the cited passages.
